To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The zeta number is the natural halting probability and is related to Chaitin's Omega number; 2) The zeta function is related to Chomsky's program-size complexity; 3) A universal Turing machine can be constructed that halts for a random sequence of inputs; 4) The zeta numbers of universal Turing machines are random and can be computed by an algorithm; 5) There exist universal Turing machines that halt for all but a random sequence

(1) the natural halting probability is a new type of randomness that is related to, but distinct from, the halting probability; (2) the natural complexity is a new type that is related to but distinct from the program-size complexity; (3) the natural halving probability is related to the halving probability; (4) a new type of partial (algorithmic) random sequence, the asymptotic random sequence, is introduced; (5) the natural complexity admits a characterization
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to algorithmic randomness.
the study of the complexity and randomness of natural phenomena.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the context of Turing machine computability, the natural halting probability (or natural complexity) of a Turing machine is the most fundamental and natural measure of the randomness or partial randomness of the machine.
, in a certain sense, the natural complexity of a machine can be viewed as the natural counterpart of the algorithmic complexity of a string.
the halting probability of a universal tuatar machine is a computably random number.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the zeta function can be used to define a natural halting probability and a natural complexity measure for a Turing machine and to define new notions of randomness and partial randomness.
we have shown that natural halting probability and natural complexity are more natural than Chaitin's Ω and program-size complexity, and they are more powerful than plain complexity.
the zeta numbers of the machines in the three classes (divergent, convergent, tuatara) are, respectively, random, c.e. random, and asymptotically random.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the zeta function of a Turing machine is an important and natural measure of the complexity of the machine.
we have introduced a new type of partial algorithmic randomness, asymptotic algorithmic randomness.
the zeta numbers of Turing machines are more natural and more interesting than their halting probabilities.
